column2: Corporate Philanthropy Is Out of Vogue, Now What?
column4: [This blog was adapted from remarks given at the Social Innovation Summit on June 5, 2024. You can watch the full video here.] As economic uncertainties loom, many companies are pulling back on their social commitments.
column13:
[This blog was adapted from remarks given at the Social Innovation Summit on June 5, 2024. You can watch the full video here.]
Navigating the peaks and valleys of corporate philanthropy? Swiftcurrent Valley, Glacier National ... [+] Park, Montana, 2013. (Photo by Buddy Mays/Getty Images).
As economic uncertainties loom, many companies are pulling back on their social commitments. Corporate philanthropy leaders, who often feel like an army of one inside their companies already, are having to once again prove their value. To my peers, I’m here to say: Hang on, the course will correct. The value of philanthropy will be recognized once again. Corporate philanthropy, when used strategically, is too valuable to be sidelined.
Company Leaders will Look Again to Philanthropy as a Tool for Engaging Community. We cannot take our foot off the gas just because the pendulum has swung in the other direction. Because pressing pause will set you way back when the pendulum swings back.
So, how can corporate philanthropy leaders navigate these challenging times? Here are three strategies that have proven effective:
Build Financial Resilience
Befriend your CFO. Seriously. We know philanthropic impact can take years to materialize, which is squarely at odds with the quarterly business cycles many of you are tied to. So, it's crucial to insulate philanthropic efforts from these cycles. By forging a strong relationship with your CFO, you can ensure that your philanthropic initiatives are on their radar, especially during financial transactions like public offerings, mergers, or real estate sales. These events provide opportunities to secure funding for your initiatives. Also consider establishing structures that offer more financial insulation. Setting up a foundation (if you don’t have one) or creating an endowment (if you do) can protect you from annual budget pressures. Hybrid models, such as LLCs, can provide flexibility and reduce conflicts of interest.
Lean into Areas with Strategic Alignment to the Business
Philanthropy has a strategic value to your company, so lean in and make the bets you know will be valued by the business. Can your philanthropy support talent pipelines, bring you into new, priority markets, or drive R&D for products that fill important needs for underserved communities? Your philanthropic capital is your highest-risk capital—use it to innovative to benefit the community and the business. For example, Walmart has invested in regenerative agriculture through its foundation, integrating those insights into its core business. Expedia Group (an APCO client) supports small businesses focused on inclusive travel through its Open World Accelerator program, fostering new partnerships and ideas that benefit the company, while creating better travel experiences for underserved travelers who often face barriers.
Engage Communities in Decision-Making
During the pandemic, the push towards trust-based philanthropy gained traction, galvanizing funders to give unrestricted funding, reduce reporting requirements, and bring community voices into the heart of their decision-making. Yet corporate philanthropy has been slow to embrace these shifts and where they have, we see some are walking back. Companies are creatures of risk mitigation, making it hard to tolerate the uncertainty inherent to social change grantmaking and to let go of the reigns of decision-making. But I would argue there is a way to do this that not only mitigates risk but also generates significant upside. From the ideas and learnings we get when we are entrenched in community design and implementation to the rich and deep storytelling that emerges when communities are powerfully stewarding our resources: these stories and learnings - when they make their way back to your board and c-suite - become powerful accelerants for your work.
By building financial resilience, leveraging strategic value, and deeply engaging with communities, philanthropy leaders can sustain their efforts and ensure they remain impactful, even in challenging times.

Venkatesan will report to PayPal President and CEO Alex Chriss and oversee technology development and implementation across the PayPal ecosystem, including analytics, data science, artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, information security, infrastructure operations, and product engineering.

column2: Target Is Rolling Out a New AI Tool. Retailers Are Embracing the Technology.
column4: Target plans to roll out its new AI-powered chatbot across its 2,000 stores by August. Target is scaling up its artificial intelligence capabilities, becoming the latest retailer to dive headfirst into the AI hype.
column13:
By

Sabrina Escobar

Target is scaling up its artificial intelligence capabilities, becoming the latest retailer to dive headfirst into the AI hype.
The retailer’s new tool, Store Companion, is a generative AI chatbot that will give store employees immediate answers about store processes and procedures. For example, staff members can ask the chatbot questions about how to sign up a customer for a loyalty card, or how to reboot the cash register in the event of a power outage. The tool will also help onboard new employees, Target said. 
“The...

Courtesy Target Corporation

Target
            

      is scaling up its artificial intelligence capabilities, becoming the latest retailer to dive headfirst into the AI hype.
The retailer’s new tool, Store Companion, is a generative AI chatbot that will give store employees immediate answers about store processes and procedures. For example, staff members can ask the chatbot questions about how to sign up a customer for a loyalty card, or how to reboot the cash register in the event of a power outage. The tool will also help onboard new employees, Target said. 
“The tool frees up time and attention for our team to serve guests with care and to create a shopping destination that invites discovery, ease and moments of everyday joy,” said Mark Schindele, Target’s executive vice president and chief stores officer. 
Target is currently piloting the chatbot at about 400 stores, and expects to roll it out nationwide by August. The company plans to release a few other generative AI products in the coming months, particularly tools that improve its e-commerce capabilities. Generative AI will summarize online customer reviews, improve product descriptions, and provide more relevant search results, Target said. 
Since the rollout of ChatGPT about two years ago, retailers have been looking for ways to integrate generative AI into their business models. The industry has used some form of AI for years in demand forecasting, supply-chain logistics, and online-shopping algorithms. 
But generative AI is expected to usher in a new era of productivity across retail, as Barron’s previously reported. Gen AI uses advanced machine learning to better mimic human intelligence, allowing it to create text, images, sound, video, and more. 
McKinsey estimates that the retail and consumer-goods sector could see productivity gains of up to $660 billion a year once the technology ramps up, as it will help streamline processes from customer service and marketing to supply chain management. AI could also help with long-term margin and profit growth, experts say. 
It isn’t surprising, then, that retailers have been fielding more questions from investors about how they’re incorporating the technology—and that retailers in turn are rushing to tout any gains made. Mentions of artificial intelligence in company filings, news releases, and conference calls have increased steadily across the industry in the past few quarters. 

Signet Jewelers
,

      for instance, said in its latest quarterly report that it hopes AI—along with financial discipline and sourcing efficiencies—will help it deliver approximately $150 million to $180 million in new cost savings in fiscal 2025, as well as help it increase market share in the jewelry sector. 

        CEO Tom Siebel spoke about the how artificial intelligence will affect communication, journalism, legal careers, and medicine as part of a wide-ranging conversation.
        
        
        Barron's Online
        

And at an investor conference in June, fashion retailer

            Revolve Group


Advertisement - Scroll to Continue





      said it was using generative AI to produce editorial images and to fine-tune its online search algorithms. The company is also using AI to improve back-end efficiency, such as answering customer service emails and improving warehouse inventory processes.
Larger companies, including

            Walmart
,
Lowe’s
,

      and

            Home Depot
,

      have also invested in scaling their AI capabilities. Even

            Costco Wholesale
,

      which has been slow at adopting new technologies in the past, has told investors it is exploring potential AI applications as it bolsters its e-commerce business. 
“Although generative AI is in the early innings of its developments, we see a world of opportunities for retailers and restaurants to leverage AI to increase conversion, build bigger baskets, and optimize costs ahead,” wrote a group of Jefferies analysts in a June 7 note. 
It will take some time, however, for many of these initiatives to start delivering returns for investors. Most retailers are still fine-tuning their AI strategies and working through implementation challenges. These include lack of consumer trust in AI, concerns over data privacy and protection, and hefty costs.

column2: Bitcoin's Slump May Be Contagious. Nvidia and Big Tech Could See a Summer Swoon.
column4: Bitcoin has caught a bit of an early summer sniffles. Will the stock market catch its cold? The world's most valuable cryptocurrency has pulled back about 9% since rallying to above $71,000 earlier this month. Now, it is hovering just below $65,000.
column13:
By

Paul R. La Monica

Bitcoin has caught the early summer sniffles. Will the stock market catch its cold?
The world’s most valuable cryptocurrency has pulled back about 9% since rallying to above $71,000 earlier this month. Now, it is hovering below $65,000. That could be a bad sign for the broader market, warns Barry Bannister, chief equity strategist with Stifel.
Bannister...

Stifel’s Barry Bannister is concerned that the recent crypto pullback is a warning sign for the tech-heavy S&P 500.

The world’s most valuable cryptocurrency has pulled back about 9% since rallying to above $71,000 earlier this month. Now, it is hovering below $65,000. That could be a bad sign for the broader market, warns Barry Bannister, chief equity strategist with Stifel.
Bannister is concerned that since 2020 “excess liquidity in the wake of the large Covid handouts has caused Bitcoin to correlate with the

As such, Bannister suggested in a report Thursday that “the weakeningof Bitcoin signals an imminent S&P 500 summer correction.” He argues that Bitcoin had rallied (and that big tech stocks are still rallying) on hopes of rate cuts by the Federal Reserve over the next few months. But he isn’t convinced that inflation pressures will cool enough to justify easing just yet.
“The correction we expect in risk assets…is furthered by our view that the Fed shifts away from its current cautious dovishness as inflation remains high…thereby exposing the overvalued S&P 500,” he wrote.
Bannister’s bearishness may be warranted. But he’s part of a relatively small crowd of market cynics on Wall Street. Many other strategists are rushing to raise their price targets for the stock market, reflecting hopes that the Fed may soon begin cutting interest rates and that earnings growth will remain relatively strong. Investors are clearly believers in the argument for an economic soft landing.
Morgan Stanley’s Mike Wilson, a prominent market skeptic, recently threw in the towel on his call for a big drop for stocks. And Julian Emmanuel of Evercore ISI has even suggested the S&P 500 could hit a new high of 6,000 by year-end.
But even Bannister concedes that a 6,000 target for the S&P 500 is possible. He just worries about what will happen after that. Hype about artificial intelligence continues to lift shares of chip giant Nvidia and those of other large-cap techs to dizzying new highs. That may not last, though.
A morning briefing on what you need to know in the day ahead, including exclusive commentary from Barron's and MarketWatch writers.
“We are aware that investors may be in full-fledged bubble/mania mode which looks past our concerns,” Bannister wrote, comparing AI to the internet stock bubble of the late 1990s. He said the current AI rally could push the S&P 500 to 6,000 by the end of the year but that he expects the blue chip index to potentially tumble all the way back t0 4,800 by early 2026 as the hype recedes.
Of course, there are others who share Bannister’s concerns about how the stock market (and U.S. economy for that matter) could be nearing a top. Another investment strategist recently suggested that the relative strength of shares of discount retailer

            Walmart
            

      could be a warning sign for a possible recession, as consumers shift their shopping patterns to hunt for more bargains.
And strategists at Ned Davis Research pointed out in a report earlier this week that “while there’s been no shortage of headlines about the latest record highs on the S&P 500 and Nasdaq, the highs have been less significant as a sign of market strength than as an influence on investor sentiment.” They noted that many other global market indexes and “other broad market barometers reflect trend conditions that are no better than neutral.”
The Ned Davis strategists are particularly worried about how narrow the current stock market rally is. “There’s currently little to suggest that the breadth of new highs will be confirming the benchmark highs any time soon,” they wrote.
So while the titans of tech may keep propping up equities in the U.S. for a little while longer, investors have to look under the surface and continue to keep an eye on Bitcoin and global stock markets for potential signs of weakness.

column2: Is GameStop Worth Buying Now?
column4: Is GameStop Stock Worth Buying Now? Forbes ...
column13:
GameStop is probably the most famous meme stock.
The GameStop (GME) roller coaster sprung to life again in May, driving a 385% stock price gain in two weeks. More than two-thirds of the lift evaporated just as quickly. Even so, the surge may have prompted your inner thrill-seeker to wonder if GameStop stock is worth a look.
To answer that question, let's explore what's happening with the gaming retailer and the risks involved in becoming a GameStop shareholder.
GameStop sells video games and hardware on its website and through 4,413 retail stores around the world. The chain has top positioning for in-store video game purchases, beating out Walmart and Best Buy. However, an ongoing shift to online gaming and downloadable games is eroding GameStop's revenue opportunity.
To quantify that erosion, GameStop's annual sales in 2023 were $5.2 billion, 42% lower than 2011 annual sales of $9 billion. The company's annual sales in 2020, when the Covid-19 pandemic temporarily shuttered stores, was $5.0 billion—only slightly lower than last year's performance.
Historical stock prices have been adjusted for GME's 4:1 stock split in July 2022.
Between 2015 and 2020, GME stock slid from $11 per share to less than $1 per share. In early 2021, GameStop spiked to $80. The catalyst was meme stock investor Richard Gill, who promoted GME on YouTube and Reddit. Over the next three years, GME's price took a rocky path downward, hitting about $11 in April of this year. Meanwhile, Gill had fallen silent on social media.
On May 12, Gill resurfaced, posting an image to his X account under his handle Roaring Kitty. The image was a sketch of a man sitting in a chair, holding something that looked like a video game controller. This sudden return of Roaring Kitty sparked a new interest in GME and the stock surged in response.
More posts from Gill followed. Some included screenshots indicating he owned 5 million GME shares plus 120,000 call options. He also made a livestream appearance on YouTube, saying he believed GME CEO Ryan Cohen might be able to turn the company around.
Between early-May and mid-June, GME traded as high as $48.75 before dipping down to about $25.
The brain trust at Forbes has run the numbers, conducted the research, and done the analysis to come up with some of the best places for you to make money in 2024. Download Forbes' most popular report, 12 Stocks To Buy Now.
GameStop's most recent balance sheet dated May 4, 2024, included more than $1 billion in cash and marketable securities. The long-term debt balance was just shy of $15 million. Operating leases and other long-term debt totaled about $400 million.
After the balance sheet date, GME's leadership team took advantage of Roaring Kitty's return to sell shares and raise cash. In two equity offerings, GameStop generated proceeds of more than $3 billion. That raises GameStop's cash position to about $4 billion.
The company's income statement performance is less impressive. First quarter 2024 net sales fell 40% from the prior-year quarter. The quarterly net loss, however, improved to $32.3 million from $50.5 million.
For the fiscal year 2023, GameStop generated net sales of $5.2 billion, down 12% from $5.9 billion in the prior year. The company did deliver net income of $6.7 million, up from a net loss of $313 million in the prior year.
GameStop currently has a yield of zero. The company hasn’t paid a dividend since March 2019.
For the past nine months, GameStop has shared little about the ongoing business, outside of two equity sales announcements and regular earnings releases. The company has not held an earnings conference call in more than a year.
In other words, there is no "official" news driving the stock's recent volatility. The primary reasons GME stock spiked briefly were the return of Gill and his show of support for the company and its CEO.
GameStop did host its annual shareholders' meeting on June 17. Cohen's opening remarks referenced cost reductions, a focus on profitability, a smaller network of stores and long-term shareholder value. The stock price opened the day at $28.90 and fell to $25.22 by close of trading.

GameStop faces two major challenges: changing consumer preferences and a questionable ability to execute.
GameStop's primary asset is a chain of brick-and-mortar stores that sell video games and hardware. Unfortunately, gamers are increasingly going online to buy, access and play games. This disconnect between what GameStop offers and how its customers shop has been escalating for years.
Between 2016 and 2019, GameStop's leadership team made various turnaround moves, which included strategic acquisitions and a plan called GameStop Reboot. None of these efforts solved GameStop's problems.
In 2021, GameStop announced the appointment of Cohen as executive chairman. Two years later, Cohen stepped in as GameStop CEO. Cohen's venture capital firm was GameStop's largest shareholder at the time. Cohen's résumé included the founding of e-commerce company Chewy in 2011.
Cohen has detailed the company's strategy. The income statement shows cost and margin improvements. And there was quick decision-making required to capitalize on the recent stock surge to raise funds. But it's unclear if GameStop is doing anything else to change its fate. With the lack of transparency plus revenues that just keep falling, it appears the company has an execution problem.
An inability to execute is a death sentence for GameStop, no matter how much cash sits on the balance sheet. Even if the company uses its newfound funding to acquire profitable businesses, running and growing those new assets cannot be done well without solid implementation skills.
The only analyst currently covering GameStop is Michael Pachter at Wedbush. Pachter has a sell rating on GME and recently lowered his price target to $11 from $13.50.
In an interview with CNBC, Pachter famously called the 2021 GME stock rally a “pyramid scheme.” Pachter's price target was $16 at the time.
The price of GME fell after the company opened its shareholder presentation—signaling that investors were largely unimpressed.
Sentiment within the GameStop-focused subreddit r/Superstonk has been split. Some have faith GameStop will rise again, citing the company's improved balance sheet. Others point out, rightfully so, that Cohen shared no specific plans for a turnaround.
GameStop is a gamble, even for the hardiest of investors. The primary issue is the lack of communication from the leadership team about the company's go-forward plan. Without those details, the stock price will continue to be driven by social media posts and meme stock investors. Those drivers are unpredictable and create more volatility than most investors are willing to accept.
GameStop has a bunch of cash, no debt and a dying business model. To be fair, there may be turnaround opportunities involving acquisitions and/or organic growth initiatives. Unfortunately, silence from the leadership team about the company's future is a dealbreaker. There are too many other good companies out there to put money in a stock that requires so much blind faith.
GameStop's stock price surged in 2021 after meme stock investor Keith Gill and a Reddit forum called r/wallstreetbets rallied the public to buy the stock and force a short squeeze. Hedge funds and other investors who had bet on the gaming retailer's failure incurred losses as the stock price rose. 
GameStop announced a turnaround plan in 2019 called GameStop Reboot. The plan included two priorities relative to the digital gaming trend: become the social/cultural hub for gaming and build a frictionless digital ecosystem. The company stopped reporting on its progress under the Reboot plan in 2020, though it did launch an NFT marketplace in 2022. Beyond that effort, it's unclear how GameStop has adapted to the popularity of online gaming. 
GameStop's strategic plan and the stock's extreme volatility that's largely unrelated to business fundamentals.

CHICAGO, June 20, 2024 /PRNewswire/ -- Brown Gibbons Lang & Company is pleased to announce GENDA Inc. Headquartered in Tokyo, Japan, GENDA is an entertainment company that aims to increase the "total volume of fun" around the world through its diversified range of business activities, including amusement arcade, karaoke, food and beverage, character merchandising, and content & promotion. GENDA's platforms include GiGO and the karaoke chain BanBan, as well as mini locations of non-staffed gaming areas in Japan, North America, mainland China, the UK, and across the Middle East.
Kiddleton, an operator in GENDA's mini-location business in the U.S., has more than 400 locations that offer small Japanese-style prize machines (arcade games designed to win prizes) and prizes with Japanese-style "Kawaii" designs, which were previously unavailable in the U.S. market. GENDA is developing its business with a unique focus on "products and experiences that can only be obtained here."
NEN is a leading operator and provider of amusement vending machines, including skill cranes, bulk vending, "kiddie" games, and video games across approximately 8,000 locations in the United States. NEN boasts a large network of grocery and retail customers in the U.S., including Walmart, Kroger, and Denny's. GENDA anticipates integrating the NEN acquisition with Kiddleton's existing expertise, which features sales per location three times higher than NEN's. The integration will include NEN's maintenance networks, streamlined operations for cash collection and prize replenishment, prize and equipment procurement synergies, the rollout of additional credit card readers, and the promotion of digital membership programs. Amazon Prime Day is a summer sale that was first introduced in 2015. At the time, it was a one-day event meant to celebrate the company’s 20th anniversary. Since then, the sale has transformed into a two-day, annual affair in which Amazon offers major discounts on thousands of products. Since 2022, the e-tailer has also hosted an October Prime Day, though that’s not its official name.
Prime Day 2024 started July 16 and rans until 3:00 a.m. EDT on July 18. This was a week later than anticipated—the event usually happens during the second week of July, though the retailer has deviated before. Shoppers had about 48 hours to shop the official sale, but some items remain discounted after the official event ended.
Technically, there’s only one Prime Day each year. But for the past two years, Amazon has run a similar savings event in October. This year, Amazon also hosted its first-ever Big Spring Sale Event, adding to its annual sale repertoire yet again. Time will tell whether it becomes a tradition as well.
No, Amazon Prime Day isn’t a sitewide sale. Still, when Prime Day was running, you could find hundreds of thousands of discounts across nearly all product categories from brands like Sony, Allbirds, Kiehl’s and, of course, Amazon itself. Just keep in mind that you have to be a Prime member to take advantage of the deals.
Many retailers offer their own Prime Day-adjacent sales. Nordstrom ran its annual Anniversary Sale to coincide with Prime Day and Walmart offered thousands of deals as well. Similarly, Target hosted a two-day sale event and Best Buy ran a Black Friday in July promotion.
In recent years, individual brands and smaller businesses have also started participating in Prime Day. Whenever Prime Day is running, we suggest keeping an eye on your favorite retailers’ sites to make sure you’re getting the best deals possible.

With thousands of enticing deals available, it can be easy to end up making some unnecessary impulse buys over Prime Day. If you’re looking to curb your spending, be sure to make a wish list of items you know you need before you start scrolling through the offers. That way, you can navigate straight to the items you’re looking for (and be less likely to forget anything, too).
Sometimes Amazon will inflate the original price of an item to make a deal look better than it really is. To avoid falling for that, try Googling the item’s Black Friday or Prime Day 2023 price to get an idea of what it’s sold for in the past. You can also use a price history tracking site like CamelCamelCamel to get an idea of what the product typically goes for.
Amazon typically releases new deals on the second day of the sale. Make sure to check out those offers, otherwise you could be missing out on some good deals.
